extracted.intended_audience: Researchers, early-career faculty, university administrators, and NYC youth-service nonprofits seeking grants to reduce inequality
extracted.subtask_description: Describes the William T. Grant Foundation's grant supports for work aimed at reducing inequality, including the types of projects and applicants the foundation funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for field-initiated research
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports research projects that are initiated by researchers working in the field (i.e., investigator-initiated studies) focused on reducing inequality. (No further detail provided on this page.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Career-development for early-career faculty
rubrics_metrics.description: Our grants support career-development for early-career faculty
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding is available to support career development activities for early-career faculty whose work relates to reducing inequality. (No further detail provided on this page.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional change at universities
rubrics_metrics.description: Our grants support institutional change at universities
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants can fund efforts aimed at producing institutional-level change within universities to address or reduce inequality. (No further detail provided on this page.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Projects to strengthen youth service nonprofits in New York City
rubrics_metrics.description: Our grants support projects to strengthen youth service nonprofits in New York City
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding targets projects that build capacity or otherwise strengthen youth-service nonprofit organizations located in New York City, with the goal of reducing inequality. (No further detail provided on this page.)
